objective: 0.3.0 pi 5/10: Support Kimi for Coding (global) as the first model provider of the Pi integration, so a Pi session and its specialists run on it, leaving other providers as later work.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.

The provider is reached only through Pi's own provider layer, with the model chosen by --model <provider/id>:<thinking> or set_model and set_thinking_level; HolyAgent never calls provider URLs, never reads auth.json and never uses pi auth print-api-key or print-bearer-token.

Before launching a root or specialist, readiness is checked with pi auth check --provider <id> --json (exit 0 ready, 1 not_ready, 2 invalid); a not-ready provider is reported as a blocker with the fix and is never silently replaced.
Model ids are validated at launch against the user's catalog (pi --list-models or get_available_models), not hard-coded.
Provider choice is isolated behind one mapping from route-table model and effort to provider/id and thinking level; no other provider is implemented or documented as supported in 0.3.0.
docs/pi/providers.md (or a new page) gains the Kimi for Coding facts the integration relies on: provider id, login, model ids used, thinking levels, the route-table mapping.

Sessions and specialists that run on Kimi K3.1 through Kimi for Coding (global) load the Kimi K3.1 instruction set from Intent 0.3.0 pi 3/10, not the Claude 5.5 set.

Maintainer (verbatim): "check if there is any already existent and maintained pi extension for full kimi for coding global integration". Research (2026-11-07) found pi-provider-kimi-code by Leechael (https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code, MIT, v0.6.13 on 2026-10-05, about nine releases since 2026-07-16, tracks pi 0.99.2), layered on pi's built-in kimi-coding provider (api.kimi.com/coding, anthropic-messages API, KIMI_API_KEY or Kimi Code OAuth). Per the existing-extensions rule, the integration installs and pins that extension rather than building a provider.

What it supplies, per its README: OAuth login shared with the official kimi-code CLI plus a KIMI_API_KEY fallback, region switching through KIMI_CODE_REGION, Files API uploads for large images, tool-schema dedup under Moonshot's 15 KB per-tool limit, quota display from /usages, prompt-cache key and reasoning-level mapping, and optional Moonshot-side tools (moonshot_search, moonshot_fetch, kimi_datasource).

Open: which host is the global Kimi for Coding endpoint (the extension's README says api.kimi.ai is global and api.kimi.com mainland, while the built-in uses api.kimi.com); verify and set KIMI_CODE_REGION explicitly.
Open: whether Kimi K3.1 is served through Kimi for Coding and under which model id; the sources list k3, kimi-for-coding and kimi-for-coding-highspeed.

Open: whether to enable the extension's Moonshot-side tools, which send data to Moonshot's services; the extension's open issue #16 on tool schemas; and its single-maintainer risk (fallback: the built-in kimi-coding provider).
